examples.ko: 이 작가의 새 소설이 다음 주에 출간돼요.
examples.en: This author's new novel is being published next week.

examples.ko: 그 책은 십 년 전에 출간됐어요.
examples.en: That book was published ten years ago.

examples.ko: 번역본이 출간되면 꼭 사서 읽을 거예요.
examples.en: When the translation is published, I'll definitely buy and read it.
The poetry collection published this time is popular in bookstores.
A signing event is held on the day the book is published.

examples.ko: 외국에서 먼저 출간된 뒤에 한국에도 들어왔어요.
examples.en: It was first published abroad and then came to Korea.

explain: 책이 세상에 나올 때 써요. 신문이나 잡지 같은 정기 간행물은 '발행되다', 책은 '출간되다', '출판되다'를 써요. '출간되다'는 막 나온 새 책 소식에 특히 자주 써요.

phrases.en: That novel was published this spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: '출간되다'와 거의 같은 뜻이지만 책을 만들어 내는 일 전체를 가리키는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 출간되다, but it feels like the whole process of producing a book.

phrases.en: I want to buy the book that came out yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갓 나온 책을 꾸미는 모양으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as a modifier for a newly released book.

phrases.example: 그 작가의 새 책이 다음 달에 나와요.
phrases.en: The author's new book comes out next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '출간되다' 대신 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday way to say 출간되다.

explain_en: Used when a book comes out into the world. Periodicals like newspapers and magazines are 발행되다, while books are 출간되다 or 출판되다. 출간되다 is especially common for news of a newly released book.

dis.h: a book comes out; common in publisher news
gh: a book gets printed and released

p.n: Almost the same; 출판 is the more general word.

examples.en: The sound of the harp is really clear and soft.
I want to learn the harp someday.

examples.ko: 무대 가운데에 큰 하프가 놓여 있었어요.
examples.en: A big harp was placed in the middle of the stage.
The harpist slowly plucked the strings.
This piece is played on the harp and the piano.
A harp is large, so it's hard to move.

explain: 발음이 같은 '하프(half)'는 '하프타임'처럼 절반을 뜻하는 다른 말이라서 문맥으로 구분해요. 악기 하프는 손가락으로 줄을 튕겨 소리를 내며 '하프를 연주하다'라고 말해요. 활로 줄을 켜는 바이올린과는 소리를 내는 방법이 달라요.

phrases.en: She plays the harp on stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기 하프와 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with the instrument.

phrases.en: Hearing the harp makes me feel calm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기의 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the sound of the instrument.

phrases.en: I learn the harp every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기를 공부한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you are studying the instrument.

explain_en: The identically pronounced 하프 (half) is a different word meaning 'half', as in 하프타임, so context tells them apart. The harp is played by plucking the strings with the fingers, and you say 하프를 연주하다. This differs from the violin, whose strings are played with a bow.

examples.en: At today's concert they'll play a piano concerto.
That violinist played a Beethoven concerto.
A concerto is played by a soloist and an orchestra together.
I study while listening to a Mozart concerto.

examples.ko: 이 협주곡의 마지막 악장이 제일 빨라요.
examples.en: The last movement of this concerto is the fastest.
I like symphonies more than concertos.

explain: '피아노 협주곡', '바이올린 협주곡'처럼 악기 이름이 앞에 와요. 혼자 연주하는 '독주곡'이나 여러 악기가 함께하는 '교향곡'과 달라요. 한국어로는 '콘체르토'보다 '협주곡'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I like piano concertos.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기 이름이 앞에 오는 가장 흔한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, with the instrument name first.

phrases.en: I listened to a violin concerto today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 악기 이름으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can swap in other instrument names.

phrases.en: The orchestra plays a concerto.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공연 장면에서 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used in concert settings.

explain_en: The instrument name comes first, as in '피아노 협주곡' and '바이올린 협주곡'. It differs from a solo piece, '독주곡', and from a symphony, '교향곡'. In Korean people say '협주곡' rather than '콘체르토'.

en: to dart one's tongue in and out

examples.en: That snake over there keeps flicking its tongue.

examples.ko: 강아지가 물을 마실 때 혀를 날름거리면서 마셔요.
examples.en: The puppy laps up water, flicking its tongue.
It was fascinating to watch the lizard flick its tongue.
Flames flickered inside the stove.
Don't flick your tongue around; eat politely.
The child flicked out his tongue at the sight of the ice cream.

explain: 혀나 불길이 자꾸 빠르게 나왔다 들어갔다 하는 모습에 써요. '날름대다'와 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The dog laps up water, flicking its tongue.
phrases.nuance_ko: '날름거리다'와 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 날름거리다 and interchangeable with it.

phrases.en: The snake's darting tongue was scary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 이렇게 바꿔 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.en: Flames flicker in the stove.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혀뿐 아니라 불길이 빠르게 일렁일 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can describe flames flickering quickly, not only tongues.

explain_en: Use it when a tongue or flame keeps darting in and out quickly. It can be swapped with '날름대다' with the same meaning.

examples.en: When spring comes, pussy willows bloom by the brook.
When I touched the pussy willow, it was soft like down.
The children played holding pussy willow twigs they had snapped off.
The fluffy pussy willow is really cute.

examples.ko: 이른 봄에 버들강아지를 보면 기분이 좋아져요.
examples.en: Seeing pussy willows in early spring makes me feel good.
The pussy willow in the photo sparkles in the sunlight.

explain: 진짜 강아지가 아니라 이른 봄에 버드나무 종류에 피는 솜털 같은 꽃이삭이에요. 봄이 오는 것을 알리는 모습으로 말할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: White catkins bloomed by the stream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버들강아지와 같은 식물을 부르는 다른 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another name for the same plant as 버들강아지.

phrases.en: Catkins have sprouted on every branch.
phrases.nuance_ko: '피다'보다 막 올라오는 모습을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits better than 피다 when describing them just emerging.

phrases.en: In spring, I picked some catkins and put them in a vase.
phrases.nuance_ko: 봄에 버들강아지를 가져다 장식할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when picking catkins to decorate with in spring.

explain_en: Despite the name, it is not a puppy but the fuzzy, downy flower spike that appears on willow trees in early spring. It fits well when talking about the arrival of spring.

examples.en: There is a crater at the top of Hallasan.
Water collected in the crater and became a lake.
I want to see a volcano's crater up close.
It is dangerous to go inside the crater.
There is a big lake in the crater of Baekdusan.
Smoke rose from the crater.

explain: 화산 분화구에 물이 고이면 '화구호'라고 해요. 백두산 천지가 가장 유명한 예예요. 달 표면의 둥근 구덩이는 '크레이터'라는 말을 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I looked down at the crater from the top of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산꼭대기에서 분화구를 볼 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for viewing a crater from the summit.
phrases.en_equiv: to look down into the crater

phrases.en: White smoke is coming out of the crater.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화산이 활동할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a volcano is active.
phrases.en_equiv: smoke comes out of the crater

phrases.example: 화산이 터진 뒤에 산꼭대기에 큰 분화구가 생겼어요.
phrases.en: After the volcano erupted, a big crater formed at the top of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화산이 폭발한 뒤 산꼭대기가 깊고 둥글게 파인 곳이 생길 때 써요. 화산이 아닌 곳의 구덩이는 '크레이터'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a deep round hollow forms at a volcano's summit after an eruption. For hollows not made by a volcano, 크레이터 is used.

explain_en: When water collects in a volcanic crater it is called a 화구호 (crater lake), and Baekdusan's 천지 is the best-known example. For the round pits on the moon, the word 크레이터 is used more often.

examples.en: I got bitten by red ants in the mountains and it hurt a lot.

examples.ko: 불개미가 집 앞 화단에 줄지어 다녀요.
examples.en: Red ants are walking in a line in the flower bed in front of my house.

examples.ko: 불개미는 나무 밑에 집을 짓고 살아요.
examples.en: Red ants build nests under trees and live there.
If a red ant bites you, it stings and swells.
I was startled to see a swarm of red ants.
I sprayed insecticide to get rid of the red ants.

explain: 붉은빛이 나는 개미를 말하고, 물리면 따끔해서 조심하라는 이야기에 자주 나와요. 뉴스에서는 외국에서 들어온 '붉은불개미'라는 이름으로 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: The news said to watch out for red fire ants.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외국에서 들어온 개미를 말할 때 뉴스에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news for ants that came from abroad.

phrases.en: I saw a swarm of red ants in the grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: '떼'를 붙이면 개미가 많이 모여 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 떼 means many ants gathered together.

phrases.en: I got bitten by ants on the mountain and it itches.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불개미'보다 넓은 '개미'를 써서 일상에서 흔하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the wider word 개미 (ant), common in daily talk.

explain_en: It refers to reddish ants, and comes up often when people warn that their bite stings. In the news it often appears under the name '붉은불개미' for the red imported fire ant.

examples.en: The cat batted the toy with its front paw.
The puppy raises its front paw to say hello.
The horse raised its front legs and neighed loudly.
I went to the clinic to treat the injured front paw.
The bear caught a fish with its front paw.
Our dog scratches the door with its front paw.

explain: 짝말은 '뒷발'이에요. 동물에게는 '손' 대신 '앞발'을 쓰고, 다리 전체를 말할 때는 '앞다리'라고 해요. 개나 고양이가 앞발로 무엇을 하는지 말할 때 '앞발로 ~하다'가 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The cat is licking its front paw.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이 앞발을 깨끗이 할 때 자주 보는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common sight when an animal cleans its front paw.

phrases.en: The horse hurt its front leg.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞발은 발 부분이고, 앞다리는 다리 전체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 앞발 is the paw; 앞다리 is the whole front leg.

phrases.en: Rabbits have long back feet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞발의 짝말이고, 동물의 뒤쪽 발을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart of 앞발; an animal's back foot.

explain_en: The paired word is '뒷발' (hind paw). For animals you say '앞발' instead of '손', and '앞다리' for the whole front leg. The pattern '앞발로 ~하다' often describes what a dog or cat does with its front paw.

en: to come and go; to move back and forth

examples.ko: 요즘 날씨가 오락가락해서 옷 입기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: The weather keeps changing these days, so it's hard to decide what to wear.
It's raining on and off, so take an umbrella.

examples.ko: 오락가락하는 태도 때문에 그 사람을 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to trust that person because of the way they keep changing their attitude.
The fever was so high that I kept drifting in and out of consciousness.
The patient keeps drifting in and out of consciousness.
The stock price fluctuated and finally went down.

explain: 비, 날씨, 기분, 정신처럼 왔다 갔다 하며 일정하지 않은 것에 써요. 단순히 오가는 동작은 '왔다 갔다 하다'라고 더 일상적으로 말해요.

phrases.en: I caught a cold because of the changeable weather.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-는' form modifies a noun that follows.

phrases.en: My mood has been up and down lately, and it's hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이나 기분이 일정하지 않고 자꾸 바뀔 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when feelings keep changing and are not steady.

phrases.en: I had a high fever and kept drifting in and out of consciousness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정신이 맑았다 흐렸다 할 때 쓰고, 아프거나 피곤할 때 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when your mind keeps going clear and foggy, often when sick or tired.
phrases.en_equiv: to drift in and out of consciousness

explain_en: It is used for things that go back and forth without staying steady, such as rain, weather, mood or consciousness. For simply moving back and forth, the more everyday expression is '왔다 갔다 하다'.

examples.en: I got a lacquer rash, and my whole body itches.
My arms turned red, maybe from a lacquer rash I got in the mountains.

examples.ko: 옻 때문에 병원에 가야 할 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think I have to go to the hospital because of the lacquer.
I'm sensitive to lacquer, so I'm careful.

examples.ko: 옻이 올랐을 때는 긁지 말고 병원에 가세요.
examples.en: When you get a lacquer rash, don't scratch it, go to the doctor.

examples.ko: 옻으로 칠한 그릇은 오래 써도 윤이 나요.
examples.en: Bowls painted with lacquer stay shiny even after long use.

explain: '옻이 오르다', '옻을 타다'가 가장 흔한 표현이에요. 옻나무를 만지거나 옻으로 만든 음식을 먹고 피부가 가려워질 때 말해요.

phrases.example: 저는 옻을 타서 옻닭을 못 먹어요.
phrases.en: I'm sensitive to lacquer, so I can't eat lacquer chicken soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옻에 몸이 민감하게 반응하는 체질을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a body that reacts sensitively to lacquer.

phrases.example: 산에서 옻나무를 만지면 가려울 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you touch a lacquer tree in the mountains, it can make you itch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옻을 얻는 나무 이름으로, 옻이 오르는 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of the tree that gives lacquer, often seen in talk about lacquer rashes.

phrases.en: I got a lacquer rash yesterday, so I went to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옻 때문에 피부에 붉은 증상이 생겼을 때 쓰는 대표적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard expression for getting a red skin reaction from lacquer.

explain_en: The most common expressions are '옻이 오르다' and '옻을 타다'. They are used when your skin gets itchy after touching lacquer trees or eating food made with them.

examples.en: When spring came, buds sprouted on every branch.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 비가 내리면 씨앗이 움트기 시작해요.
examples.en: When warm rain falls, the seeds start to sprout.

examples.ko: 두 사람 사이에 사랑이 움트는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems love is budding between the two of them.

examples.ko: 제 꿈이 움튼 곳이 바로 이 동네예요.
examples.en: This very neighborhood is where my dream first took root.

examples.ko: 이 마을에서 새로운 희망이 움트고 있어요.
examples.en: New hope is springing up in this village.
When winter ends, grass seeds also sprout underground.

explain: 식물의 싹이 나오는 일에 쓰고, 사랑·희망·생각이 처음 생겨나는 것에도 많이 써요. 비슷한 말로 '싹트다'가 있어요. 활용은 '움트다 - 움터요 - 움텄어요'예요.

phrases.en: Hope sprouted in my heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: '움트다'와 비슷하고 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '움트다' but used more commonly.

phrases.en: The sprouting buds in the spring breeze are cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 모양이고 봄 풍경을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, fitting for describing spring scenery.

phrases.en: Love began to grow between the two of them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정이 처음 생겨나기 시작할 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when a feeling first begins to form.

explain_en: It is used for plant buds coming out, and often for love, hope or ideas starting to form. '싹트다' is a similar word. The conjugation goes '움트다 - 움터요 - 움텄어요'.

en: to be steep; to be rugged; to be forbidding

examples.ko: 이 지역은 산이 험준해서 길을 내기 어려워요.
examples.en: The mountains here are rugged, so it's hard to build roads.

examples.ko: 험준한 산맥을 넘어 옆 나라로 갔어요.
examples.en: We crossed the rugged mountain range into the next country.
The terrain is rugged, so be careful when hiking.

examples.ko: 험준한 바위 길이라서 장비가 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: It's a steep, rocky path, so you definitely need gear.

examples.ko: 산이 험준해서 눈이 오면 아무도 올라가지 못해요.
examples.en: The mountain is so rugged that nobody can climb it when it snows.
It's a mountain famous for being rugged, so it's hard for beginners.

explain: 산, 지형, 길이 가파르고 거칠어서 다니기 힘들다고 할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '험하다'를 더 자주 쓰고, '험준하다'는 설명하는 글이나 뉴스, 여행 소개에서 잘 보여요. '험준한 산', '험준한 지형'처럼 함께 써요.

phrases.en: I climbed the rugged mountain path carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오르기 힘들 만큼 가파르고 거친 산을 말할 때 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for mountains steep and rough enough to be hard to climb.

phrases.example: 험준한 지형 때문에 도로를 만들기 어려워요.
phrases.en: The rugged terrain makes it hard to build roads.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설명하는 글이나 뉴스에서 지형을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in reports and news when describing terrain.

phrases.en: The mountain path was rough, so I walked slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 험준하다보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word than 험준하다 and more common in daily conversation.

explain_en: It describes mountains, terrain or paths that are steep and rough to travel. In daily talk people use '험하다' more, while '험준하다' shows up in descriptions, news and travel guides. Typical pairings are '험준한 산' and '험준한 지형'.

examples.en: I saw a bull for the first time in a country village.
A bull is really strong.
My grandfather plowed the field with an ox.
That bull suddenly ran toward us and I was startled.

examples.ko: 황소만큼 큰 개를 키우는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Someone keeps a dog as big as an ox.

examples.ko: 동상 앞에 황소 두 마리가 서 있어요.
examples.en: Two bulls are standing in front of the statue.

explain: 그냥 '소'라고 하면 암컷과 수컷 모두예요. '황소'는 크고 힘센 수컷 소, 특히 농사일을 하던 소를 말해요. 암소는 '암소', 어린 소는 '송아지'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 아버지는 황소고집이라서 한번 정하면 안 바꿔요.
phrases.en: stubbornness like an ox
phrases.nuance_ko: 한번 마음먹으면 절대 안 바꾸는 아주 센 고집을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes extreme stubbornness; someone who never changes their mind once it is made up.

explain_en: 소 on its own covers cows and bulls alike; 황소 is the big, powerful male, especially the kind used for farm work. A female is 암소 and a calf is 송아지.

examples.en: A strange rumor is going around the school.
A wild rumor spread that a ghost appears in the village.
Because of the nasty rumor, the shop has fewer customers.

examples.ko: 그런 괴소문은 믿지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better not to believe rumors like that.
We still don't know who spread the bizarre rumor.

examples.ko: 인터넷에서 가수에 대한 괴소문이 빠르게 번졌어요.
examples.en: A bizarre rumor about the singer spread quickly online.

explain: 그냥 '소문'보다 황당하고 기분 나쁜, 믿기 어려운 소문이라는 느낌이 강해요. '괴소문이 돌다/퍼지다/퍼뜨리다'처럼 써요. 무서운 이야기를 뜻하는 '괴담'과는 달라요.

phrases.en: That singer was plagued by bizarre rumors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 소문 때문에 힘들어하는 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes suffering because of nasty rumors.
phrases.en_equiv: to be plagued by odd rumors

phrases.en: I don't know who spread the odd rumor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소문을 일부러 널리 알린다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means deliberately spreading a rumor widely.

phrases.en: I've been hearing strange rumors lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉽고 가벼운 말이지만 '괴소문'만큼 황당한 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Simpler and lighter, but less absurd-sounding than 'goesomun'.

explain_en: Compared with plain '소문', it suggests an absurd, unpleasant, hard-to-believe rumor. It is used as '괴소문이 돌다/퍼지다/퍼뜨리다'. It differs from '괴담', which means a scary story.
